name: David A. Ricks

career.title: Business Development Associate; later U.S. marketing and sales management and Lilly Canada sales/marketing roles

background_rationale: Ricks rose through Lilly's commercial organization, from U.S. marketing and sales roles to running the company's Canadian, Chinese and U.S. commercial operations before leading Lilly Bio-Medicines.

notable.summary: Lilly announced a 70% list-price cut on its most commonly prescribed insulins and a $35 monthly cap on patient out-of-pocket insulin costs, with Ricks stating that the system 'does not provide affordable insulin for everyone and that needs to change.'
Lilly announced a $27 billion investment to build four new U.S. manufacturing sites, three for active pharmaceutical ingredients and one for injectable medicines.

Lilly reached an agreement with the Trump administration to lower prices of its GLP-1 obesity drugs for Medicare and direct cash purchases, in exchange for a three-year exemption from pharmaceutical tariffs.

personal_story.hook: He says he joined Eli Lilly "accidentally" in 1996. Two decades later, he was running it.
personal_story.summary: David Ricks grew up in California's East Bay, in what he calls a melting pot, and his parents took the family to live abroad. He studied industrial management at Purdue, worked at IBM and earned an MBA at Indiana University. In 1996 he joined Lilly as a business development associate largely because his girlfriend, now his wife, was in medical school — he later said he came to the company "accidentally." One project he had worked on became an approved medicine that his own mother was later prescribed, and Lilly kept moving him into jobs he says he "had no business being in," including running its businesses in Canada and China, before he became CEO in 2017.
